name: Terbutaline

lead: Terbutaline is a prescription asthma reliever that physique forums place in the same family as albuterol and clenbuterol, as a possible aid to getting leaner.

It selectively stimulates beta-2 receptors, raising cAMP, and the family is associated with higher metabolic rate. It has been studied for preventing and reversing bronchospasm; trials for fat loss or muscle have not been published.

paras: It comes as tablets and injection, and as an inhaler outside the US. In appearance discussion it is mentioned as one of several beta-2 agonists people consider for leanness. Its documented use is as an asthma reliever.

The label lists nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and fast heart rate. It carries an FDA boxed warning against use for preterm labour after maternal deaths and serious cardiac events. It is prescription-only, and WADA prohibits it except inhaled with a therapeutic use exemption.

forums.title: Minimizing Muscle Loss on 2 Wk Fast?

angle.text: Terbutaline is a beta-2 agonist that physique forums group with albuterol and clenbuterol as a route to a leaner look through a higher metabolic rate. Its studied purpose is bronchospasm in asthma.

lead: Terbutaline is a prescription selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist sold as Bricanyl, Brethine and Marex, among other names. In bodybuilding and fat-loss circles it is discussed as a stimulant-type fat-loss and pre-workout aid in the same family as albuterol (salbutamol) and clenbuterol: users describe it as a way to feel energised and, through beta-2 stimulation, to nudge metabolic rate upward while dieting toward a leaner look.[1][2]

Medically it was patented in 1966, entered use in 1970 and is indicated for preventing and reversing bronchospasm in people aged 12 and older with asthma, bronchitis and emphysema.[3][4] It has also been used off-label to delay preterm labour, which led the FDA in 2011 to add a boxed warning on injectable and oral forms.[3][4]

Human studies of terbutaline concern asthma, COPD, and obstetric and other medical uses. A small body of infusion research on beta-2 agonists in lean men, quoted in forum threads, reports modest rises in energy expenditure, but no trial has tested terbutaline as a fat-loss or muscle-gain agent.[2][5]
infobox: Prescription-only; WADA-prohibited except inhaled with TUE[4]

paras: Terbutaline is a reliever for asthma and bronchospasm; inhaled forms work within about 15 minutes. [3][4] Several classic asthma trials used it as the comparison beta-2 agonist against inhaled budesonide. [6][7]
Off-label, it has been used as a tocolytic to delay preterm labour for up to 48 hours. [4]

On T Nation, users who compare beta-2 agonists describe terbutaline as an option next to albuterol and clenbuterol for fat loss. One poster said it felt strong compared with albuterol, 'like short acting clen or more'; another said they liked albuterol or terbutaline with caffeine before training for energy, adding that these 'don't raise blood pressure much' for them.[1][8] A thread on a two-week fast cites a statement that beta-2 agonists including terbutaline could help limit muscle loss when combined with exercise.[9] These are user reports and anecdotes, not trial results.

The US label lists effects similar to other sympathomimetic amines; the Grokipedia summary of the label gives nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia as the most common. [3][10] Wikipedia lists tachycardia, anxiety, tremor, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia and rarely pulmonary edema. [4]

In February 2011 the FDA required a boxed warning that injectable terbutaline should not be used for preterm labour beyond 48 to 72 hours and oral terbutaline not at all, citing serious maternal heart problems and death. [3][4]
Its tertiary butyl group increases beta-2 selectivity, and it lacks the 4-hydroxy group that makes catecholamines susceptible to COMT. About 90% is excreted in urine. [4]

Grokipedia's summary of the label says oral effects start within roughly 30 to 120 minutes and last up to about 8 hours, with inhaled forms acting faster.[10] Wikipedia gives an elimination half-life of 11 to 16 hours and says about 90% is excreted in urine.[4] A pharmacology paper described its elimination pathways.[11]
The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits terbutaline like all beta-2 agonists, except when inhaled with a therapeutic use exemption obtained in advance. [4]

Wikipedia gives 1966 as the patent year and 1970 as the start of medical use [4]. Grokipedia says the FDA approved terbutaline on March 25, 1974 [10]. The 2011 FDA safety action against prolonged tocolytic use followed reports that Grokipedia counts as 16 maternal deaths between 1976 and 2009 [10]. In bodybuilding writing from the 2000s, terbutaline appears in threads about clenbuterol and albuterol as a less common beta-2 option [1][2].

sections.h: Reported risks in off-label physique use
paras: The common effects in the label summary, nervousness (reported in up to about a third of patients in Grokipedia's account of the label), tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia, are the same ones that forum users mention when describing stimulant-like beta-2 agonists [3][10][8]. The label cautions about cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, hyperthyroidism and low potassium, since the drug can worsen tachycardia, arrhythmia or high blood sugar [3][10]. Sports bodies treat the class as prohibited, with the exception of inhaled use under a therapeutic use exemption [4].
No clinical trial has tested terbutaline for fat loss or muscle gain. Published and registered trials concern respiratory and obstetric uses.

In asthma, a randomized blinded comparison enrolled 103 patients with newly detected asthma and compared inhaled budesonide with inhaled terbutaline over long-term treatment; the 1991 report concluded the corticosteroid was more effective than the beta-2 agonist, and a follow-up trial examined reducing or stopping budesonide and crossing patients over from terbutaline.[6][7] In a 52-week double-blind trial, adults and adolescents with mild asthma used as-needed terbutaline alone, as-needed budesonide-formoterol, or twice-daily budesonide plus terbutaline as needed; terbutaline served as the reliever comparator.[12] The PRACTICAL trial, a 52-week open-label study in New Zealand adults aged 18 to 75, compared budesonide-formoterol reliever therapy with maintenance budesonide plus as-needed terbutaline.[13]

Registered trials include a phase 3 study of 250 people comparing a beta-2 agonist with ipratropium plus beta-2 agonist in COPD exacerbations, a pilot safety study in 9 children with type 1 diabetes, and an acute tocolysis study of 100 women with suspected fetal distress.[14][15][16]

Related work on beta-2 agonist metabolism is quoted on forums: direct infusion of salbutamol and terbutaline in lean men produced a modest increase in whole-body energy expenditure, according to a passage reproduced in several T Nation threads.[2]

lore.intro: Terbutaline appears in T Nation threads about beta-2 agonist fat burners as a less common relative of clenbuterol and albuterol, often discussed alongside stimulants and caffeine.[1][8][2]

claims.claim: Terbutaline works like a short-acting clenbuterol for fat loss.
Beta-2 agonists help preserve muscle while dieting or fasting.
Terbutaline plus caffeine gives pre-workout energy with little blood-pressure effect.

timeline.event: FDA requires a boxed warning against preterm-labour use. [4]
